styles.name: Luxury Editorial
styles.summary: High-contrast serif headlines, generous margins, and one hero image per spread. Restraint signals value.
reference_sources: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (1992)

styles.name: Fashion Magazine
styles.summary: Full-bleed photography with a masthead and cover lines layered over it. The image is the layout.

styles.name: Art Direction Editorial
styles.summary: A visual concept per spread: image and type are composed together to make one idea, often with a witty crop or juxtaposition.

styles.name: Premium Product Campaign
styles.summary: A single product, lit like a sculpture, with a short line of copy and a lot of tonal background.

styles.name: Gallery and Art Catalogue
styles.summary: Artwork reproduced at true proportion on quiet pages, with small, precise captions and plate numbers.

styles.name: Swiss International Style
styles.summary: Objective grid, flush-left grotesk type, asymmetric balance, and information ordered by size and position alone.
reference_sources: Josef Müller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design (1981)

styles.name: Constructivist Layout
styles.summary: Diagonal axes, heavy bars, photomontage, and red and black blocks that push the eye in one direction.

styles.name: Brutalist Editorial
styles.summary: Exposed structure: default-looking type, visible borders, raw tables, and density over polish.

styles.name: Geometric Composition
styles.summary: Circle, square, and triangle as the main actors, in primary colors, balanced like a construction kit.

styles.name: Neoclassical Editorial
styles.summary: Symmetry, columns of text like colonnades, inscriptional capitals, and proportions borrowed from architecture.
reference_sources: Vitruvius, De architectura (1st century BCE), on symmetry and proportion

styles.name: Renaissance-Inspired Composition
styles.summary: Pyramidal grouping, a central vanishing point, and chiaroscuro light that leads the eye to one figure.

styles.name: Museum Exhibition
styles.summary: Wall-scale graphics: room numbers, timelines, and object labels designed to be read standing, at a distance, in sequence.

styles.name: Historical Poster Design
styles.summary: Interwar lithographic poster: flat stylized illustration, stepped Deco lettering in a band, and three or four flat inks.

styles.name: Oversized Type
styles.summary: One word or number set so large it is cropped by the frame. Type is the image.

styles.name: Contemporary Poster
styles.summary: A Swiss-descended grid that is deliberately broken: rotated type, layered text blocks, and one strong color field.

styles.name: Experimental Typography
styles.summary: Letterforms stretched, overlapped, distorted, or set on paths until reading becomes a deliberate act.

styles.name: Pop Graphic
styles.summary: Thick outlines, halftone dots, flat saturated fills, and comic-panel energy.

styles.name: Collage Editorial
styles.summary: Cut-out photographs, torn paper, tape, and type fragments layered to make an argument by juxtaposition.

styles.name: Swatch Card Presentation
styles.summary: Colors presented as labelled chips: a solid block above a white strip with name and code, laid out like a swatch book.

styles.name: Limited Palette
styles.summary: Two or three colors plus paper, with tints of those colors doing all the work a larger palette would.

styles.name: Complementary Color System
styles.summary: Two opposite hues: one dominant, one in small doses as the point of tension. Neutrals keep them apart.
reference_sources: Johannes Itten, The Art of Color (1961)

styles.name: Analogous Color System
styles.summary: Neighboring hues that shift gradually, like a sunset or a forest, with one deep anchor for text.
reference_sources: Johannes Itten, The Art of Color (1961)

styles.name: Monochromatic System
styles.summary: One hue across a lightness ramp. Hierarchy comes only from value, so contrast discipline is everything.

styles.name: High-Contrast Color Blocking
styles.summary: Large flat rectangles of saturated color meet at hard edges; each block holds one piece of content.

styles.name: Botanical Illustration
styles.summary: Scientific plate: one specimen drawn with fine line and wash, isolated on paper, with Latin name and plate number.

styles.name: Organic Shapes
styles.summary: Soft blobs, pebble curves, and flowing edges instead of rectangles; the container itself feels grown, not built.

styles.name: Floral Pattern
styles.summary: A repeating tile of flowers and leaves that covers a surface, with type held in a calm cartouche.

styles.name: Handcrafted Illustration
styles.summary: Visible hand: brush, pencil, or gouache marks with imperfect edges, paired with hand-lettering or a warm serif.

styles.name: Tonal Botanical
styles.summary: Leaves and stems in the same hue as the ground, a few steps darker or raised, so form reads by value and relief rather than color.

styles.name: Letterpress
styles.summary: Type and rules pressed into thick cotton paper: slight ink spread, a bitten edge, and one or two flat inks.

styles.name: Embossed Print
styles.summary: Blind emboss: shapes raised from the paper with no ink, so light and shadow alone draw them.

styles.name: Foil Stamping
styles.summary: A small metallic mark on a dark or deep-colored stock that flashes as the angle changes.

styles.name: Sculpted Surface
styles.summary: Digital clay, plaster, or stone: soft 3D relief rendered with raking light, used as a backdrop or a logo object.

styles.name: Material-Led Packaging
styles.summary: The substrate is the design: kraft, glass, uncoated board, or tin, with minimal print that lets the material show.

styles.name: Japanese-Inspired Minimalism
styles.summary: Ma: empty space as an active element, one small off-center mark, natural textures, and vertical rhythm.
reference_sources: Jun'ichiro Tanizaki, In Praise of Shadows (1933)

styles.name: Architectural Minimalism
styles.summary: Large planes of tone, hard light and shadow, monumental scale, and thin type set like a plan annotation.

styles.name: Contemporary Editorial
styles.summary: Modern publishing on screen: a serif and grotesk pairing, a flexible column grid, and generous but not extreme space.

styles.name: Minimal Product Showcase
styles.summary: Product on a seamless tone, one spec line in small type, and a strict grid of identical tiles for the range.

styles.name: Exploded View and Cutaway
styles.summary: Parts pulled apart along one axis, or a section cut open, with leader lines and numbered callouts.

styles.name: Isometric Diagram
styles.summary: Objects drawn on 30 degree axes with no perspective, so sizes stay comparable and systems read as a map.

styles.name: Product Render
styles.summary: Photoreal or clean-shaded 3D of the product under studio light, accurate materials, at a three-quarter hero angle.

styles.name: Industrial Editorial
styles.summary: Factory and process photography in a magazine grid, with specification tables and part numbers as typographic texture.

styles.name: Blueprint Diagram
styles.summary: White line drawing on blue, with a measurement grid, dimension lines, and a title block in the corner.

styles.name: Layered System Visualization
styles.summary: A system as stacked translucent planes, each one layer of the stack, with connections passing between them.

styles.name: Kinetic Typography
styles.summary: Words move in time with speech or beat: each phrase arrives, holds long enough to read, and leaves with intent.

styles.name: Morphing Shapes
styles.summary: One shape transforms into the next so the viewer sees that two ideas are the same thing in different states.

styles.name: Editorial Scene Transitions
styles.summary: Page-turn logic: an image or headline from one scene carries into the next, so sections feel like spreads of one publication.

styles.name: Camera-Driven Storytelling
styles.summary: A virtual camera moves through one continuous scene, and each stop is a chapter: establish, approach, detail, pull back.

styles.name: Scroll-Based Narrative
styles.summary: Scroll position drives the story: a sticky visual updates step by step while text panels pass over it.

styles.name: Mechanical Animation
styles.summary: Gears, pistons, and linkages move with physically correct ratios and timing so the mechanism explains itself.

styles.name: Layer Reveal
styles.summary: Layers peel, slide, or fade away in order so the viewer sees what is underneath, one level at a time.

styles.name: Data Flow Animation
styles.summary: Particles or dashes travel along paths between nodes; speed, density, and color encode real volume and state.

styles.name: 3D Product Reveal
styles.summary: The product emerges from darkness or abstraction, turns once to show its form, and settles on the hero angle.
